job.title: Fundraising Manager – Donor Acquisition (2-year contract, renewable)
job.description:
Looking for a meaningful career that allows you to
make a difference in the world?

Join Oxfam Hong Kong, a member of the Oxfam confederation, in creating a world free of poverty. As an independent development and relief agency, we work with people living in poverty and partner organisations to implement effective development, humanitarian, policy advocacy, and public education programmes.

We are seeking passionate individuals to join our team and contribute to our poverty alleviation work. Join us and be part of the solution to end poverty and create a better world for all.

Fundraising Manager – Donor Acquisition
(2-year contract, renewable) [Ref.: FCU/FRM_DA/26/01]

The Fundraising Manager is a dynamic and results-oriented professional responsible for driving donor acquisition and individual-giving growth through effective multi-channel fundraising initiatives. The role is responsible for expanding the donor base, strengthening donor engagement, and delivering sustainable income growth in support of the organisation's mission.

Key Responsibilities:
Donor Acquisition & Fundraising
  • Develop and implement donor acquisition strategies to recruit new donors and grow the supporter base.
  • Manage multi-channel donor acquisition programmes to achieve fundraising targets.
  • Drive donor recruitment, lead conversion, cash giving and monthly giving initiatives.
  • Support fundraising planning and identify opportunities for sustainable income growth.

Donor Engagement
  • Develop donor communications and acquisition materials, including direct mail, newsletters and campaign content.
  • Monitor, analyse and optimise acquisition performance, including donor conversion, acquisition costs, return on investment and donor value.
  • Lead testing and optimisation initiatives to enhance fundraising effectiveness and donor retention.
  • Oversee donor onboarding and stewardship activities to strengthen donor engagement and experience.

Operations & Team Management
  • Supervise acquisition staff, agencies and vendors to ensure effective delivery and target achievement.
  • Collaborate with internal teams and external partners on donor acquisition and stewardship initiatives.
  • Review and improve acquisition processes, workflows and operational guidelines.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant legal, ethical and organisational requirements, including data privacy and fundraising best practices.
  • Support fundraising events, campaign activities and other duties as assigned by the Director of Fundraising and Communications.
  • Overseas travel may be required.

Requirements:
  • Degree holder in Marketing, Communications, Business, Social Sciences or a related discipline.
  • At least 10 years' relevant experience in fundraising, donor acquisition, individual giving, direct and digital marketing, CRM or related fields; NGO/INGO experience is preferred.
  • Proven track record in donor acquisition, lead conversion, direct response fundraising and monthly giving programmes.
  • Solid experience in managing acquisition channels, including face-to-face fundraising, telemarketing, digital lead generation, direct mail and paid media.
  • Well-organised with strong project management skills, able to manage multiple priorities effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Good understanding of fundraising and acquisition metrics, including cost per acquisition, conversion rate, donor value and attrition.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret donor and campaign data, identify trends and recommend improvements.
  • Hands-on experience with CRM systems and donor databases; Salesforce experience is an advantage.
  • Strong donor communication, content development and copywriting skills in English and Chinese.
  • Proficient in MS Office applications, particularly Excel, and Chinese word processing.
  • Familiarity with data privacy regulations, and fundraising best practices.
  • Experience in donor retention, stewardship and supporter journey management is an advantage.
  • Excellent written and spoken English and Chinese; fluency in Putonghua is preferred.
  • Identification with Oxfam’s mission and values is a must.

Why Join Us
At Oxfam Hong Kong, our culture is shaped by our values, which reinforce what we care about and how we do things. Our five core values are: Justice, Empowerment, Inclusiveness, Accountability and Innovation. Learn more about Oxfam Hong Kong: https://www.oxfam.org.hk.

How to Apply
Closing date for application: 16 November 2026
Please send your application letter and resume, including current and expected salary and date of availability, to Human Resources Manager by email at hr@oxfam.org.hk.
---

- Proficiency in written and spoken Chinese (Cantonese and Putonghua) and English

- Assist in preparing finance reports and dashboards for manager’s review;
- Select donors for different promotion campaigns to fit for PSP operation needs;

- Import data manually when required such as data from telemarketing agencies;
- Provide technical supports with testing new functioning and operational effectiveness of the new system;

- Undertakes other duties as assigned by her/his supervisor.

Closing date: 27 October 2026

If you wish to be considered for this vacancy, please go to the link below for application (https://unhcr.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/External/job/Fundraising-System-Assistant_JR2668755?locations=113ac21cb9f410123442ebb649210000).

The appointment offer will be subject to the proof of medical clearance and satisfactory reference checks.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified and invited for the interview and written test.

job.title: Assistant Programme Officer (3 days a week)
job.description:
CantoGather is a Christian-affiliated charity founded in 2021. We work inside Hong Kong primary schools, bringing non-Chinese children, their Chinese peers and their parents together through Cantonese and intercultural learning.

Assistant Programme Officer (3 days a week)
HK$12,000 to HK$13,800 a month · 3 days a week · from November 2026

Help build a Hong Kong where every neighbour belongs! Join our small, warm and fun team to plan, teach and run real projects in primary schools. Things move fast here, so you’ll need to pick things up quickly.

Pay HK$12,000 to HK$13,800 a month plus MPF (HK$20,000 to HK$23,000 full-time equivalent)
Days Mon, Wed and Thu in person, 24 hours a week in total. It’s project-based, so you can move some of those hours to off-days for quick follow-ups.
Where Our Central office or partner schools. No work from home during probation.
Contract To 31 July 2027, renewable; 3-month probation
Start From November 2026
Reports to Senior Programme Manager

What you’ll do
• Plan lessons: write and adapt lesson plans and activities.
• Run CCC: manage our volunteer Cantonese tutors and the admin behind them.
• Teach: lead From Me to We sessions and our parent Cantonese classes.
• Work with schools: agree schedules and keep teachers in the loop.
• Keep things moving: messages, records and session set-up (yes, carrying boxes too).
A typical week: school sessions, lesson planning and volunteer coordination, with regular check-ins with your manager. The rest of the week is mostly yours.

You’ll fit right in if you’re
• Supportive: you’ve got the team’s back, just as we’ve got yours.
• Present: we know we can count on you, and find you when we need to.
• Focused: you know what matters and get it done.
• Excellent: you own your work and hold it to a high standard.
• Open: you pick things up fast and welcome feedback.

All rooted in our We CARE values: Creative & Curious, Authentic & Aware, Resilient & Responsible, Energetic & Engaging.

You’ll need
• 2 to 3 years’ work experience, especially teaching or working with people
• Fluent Cantonese and English, plus good written Chinese
• Willingness to represent and share our Christian mission and values
• Google Workspace, Microsoft Word, Excel and Canva
• Every Monday, Wednesday and Thursday free

Nice to have: teaching children Cantonese as a second language; Urdu, Hindi, Nepali, Tagalog or Punjabi.

We warmly welcome applicants of every ethnic background. If you’ve grown up between cultures in Hong Kong, that’s a real strength here.

What you’ll get
• Work that matters: help non-Chinese children feel they belong at school.
• Real ownership: run your own projects from day one, with a team that’s got your back.
• A wide skill set: teaching, lesson design, volunteer management and school partnerships, all in one role.
• Support along the way: regular check-ins with your manager, and space to try your own ideas.
• Balance: three days a week, with the rest of your week mostly yours.
• Grow with us: be part of an exciting, growing start-up, and help shape what comes next.

How to apply
Email your CV and a one-page note to recruitment@cantogather.com (subject: “Assistant Programme Officer”). Tell us why CantoGather, and one thing you ran from start to finish. Shortlisted applicants send a short video intro, then come for an interview. We’d love to hear from you!
Personal data will be used for recruitment only.

job.title: Program Associate
job.description:
Foundation for Shared Impact’s (FSI) Community Business Support Program (“CBS Program”) encompasses several projects to empower and uplift community businesses and under-resourced entrepreneurs in Hong Kong. We fulfil the CBS Program’s mission through our shared impact model, which facilitates broad cross-sector collaboration and free sharing of knowledge, information, and resources.

The CBS Program raises the visibility of grassroots small businesses through Project GuideFong, which includes an online directory of diverse community businesses, pop-up bazaars, walking tours, and digital marketing campaigns that celebrate Hong Kong’s multicultural grassroots business ecosystem while promoting diversity and social inclusion.

In parallel, the Program builds capacity for budding entrepreneurs through the Mentorship Program for Ethnically Diverse Entrepreneurs (held annually since 2022), skills workshops, pro-bono legal clinics, direct business support, and other cross-sector collaborations that connect entrepreneurs to corporate volunteers, youth interns, peer entrepreneurs, and other practical resources.

Job Description for Program Associate for Community Business Support Program (Full-time position)

FSI is seeking a motivated Program Associate to join the Community Business Support team to take the program to the next level, together with the Program Manager. This role will coordinate day-to-day delivery of CBS projects, including the Mentorship Program, Project GuideFong initiatives, manage event logistics, steward partnerships and volunteers, and curate and coordinate community-facing communications.

The role is very hands-on, requiring strong organisational and interpersonal skills, cross-cultural sensitivity, and a commitment to community-centred programming that empowers and promotes local under-resourced entrepreneurs in Hong Kong. This role demands skills and experience in program management as well as stakeholder communication and collaboration to ensure a fruitful and beneficial experience for all involved - including youths in Hong Kong whom the Program Associate will manage.

While this role will report directly to the FSI’s Community Business Support Program Manager, there will be significant collaboration with the different members of the FSI team who also support the Program, including FSI’s Executive Director, Youth Program Team, and Communications Manager.

Main Responsibilities:
● Coordinate the development, planning, and delivery of existing and new CBS initiatives in collaboration with other FSI team members.
● Oversee end-to-end program management, execution, and logistics for CBS activities.
● Design and lead GuideFong walking tours and community outreach sessions to establish rapport with ethnically diverse and grassroots small businesses and source projects for direct business support.
● Design, develop, and run the “GuideFong Ambassador” program to recruit, train, and manage youth interns and community volunteers, including those coming from underprivileged backgrounds, to support GuideFong businesses and events.
● Develop and manage Project GuideFong’s social media channels and content calendar; create or commission engaging digital content (e.g., short- and long-form videos, social media posts, business spotlights).
● Grow FSI’s CBS community, including the GuideFong directory, ensuring the accuracy and completeness of data published and shared.
● Monitor program outputs and outcomes, as well as stakeholder feedback, for impact measurement and reporting through quantitative and qualitative means.
● Perform other duties related to CBS Programs as requested by the Program Manager.

Preferred Background:
● Minimum of 2 years of working experience required.
● Experience in project management or event coordination is required.
● Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
● Excellent interpersonal communication, community engagement, and relationship-building skills, including professionalism, ease, and confidence in liaising with small business owners, youths, volunteers, and corporate partners.
● Flexibility to work occasional weekends/evenings for events.
● Responsible, proactive, committed, and driven work ethic.
● Good technology literacy and proficiency in using digital tools (or a willingness to learn how to use digital tools).
● Skills in social media management, visual design, digital marketing, content creation, photography, and/or video production are preferred.
● Fluency in written and spoken English is required; proficiency in Cantonese, Urdu, Hindi, or Nepali is a significant advantage
● Experience in working with educational institutions and youths is preferred.

Employee Benefits:
● Salary (HK$23K - HK$27K based on merit and experience) + MPF
● Up to HK$2K reimbursement under FSI’s annual personal development fund scheme
● 15 days of annual leave (excluding public holidays)
● Flexible working hours and arrangements in a hybrid workplace
● A plethora of opportunities for training and professional development
● Opportunity to broaden horizon in a multicultural environment

We are hiring a full-time staff with a contract term of 12 months, with extension subject to funding availability, performance, and assessment. If you have questions, please contact Vivian Seo, Executive Director of FSI, at vivian@shared-impact.com.

To apply, please submit your one-page cover letter and CV via email to admin@shared-impact.com by 30 October 2026, and include “Applying for the CBS Program Associate Position” in the email subject. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis (prioritizing fit and opportunities for future growth together over availability). We hope to start employment from late October to early November 2026.

About the Foundation for Shared Impact (FSI)
___________________________________________________________
FSI is a Section 88 organization dedicated to addressing society’s most challenging problems by connecting different sectors to facilitate broad collaboration and free sharing of resources, knowledge and information. Our work aims to cultivate better leaders and build resilient communities - changing the way we do business for good.

For more information on FSI and our core programs, visit our website: https://www.shared-impact.com/

Read our recently published Impact Report (2023-25): https://shared-impact.com/impactreport

The Communications Manager reports to the Director of Fundraising and Communications and supports in leading the organisation’s branding, corporate messaging, marketing and digital initiatives, as well as event-related communication activities. The role plays a key part in shaping strategic narratives and strengthening the organisation’s overall brand presence. Below are his/her key responsibilities:

· Develop and implement communications strategies to raise awareness, engagement and public support.
· Oversee brand management to ensure consistent messaging, tone of voice, visual identity and adherence to brand guidelines.

· Oversee editorial planning and content governance, including editorial calendars, approval workflows, tone of voice and quality control.
· Monitor and evaluate communication campaigns using analytics, media monitoring, social media insights and audience feedback.
· Work closely with internal teams, including Directorate, Fundraising Teams and Programme Units to develop integrated communications and ensure quality.
· Manage external vendors, agencies and production partners to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
· Coach and develop team members to strengthen communications capability and performance.

Requirements:
· Degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Marketing, Digital Media or related disciplines.
· Minimum 15 years’ relevant working experience, of which 8 years on managerial grade.
· Proven experience in communications strategy, brand management, digital/social media strategy, crisis communications and editorial planning.
· Excellent writing, editing and storytelling skills in English and Chinese.
· Strong understanding of media relations, social media platforms, digital campaigns, audience engagement and performance analytics.
· Sound judgement and experience in handling sensitive issues, reputational risks, media enquiries and public statements.
· Strong leadership, stakeholder management, project management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
· Experience in NGOs, public bodies, advocacy, fundraising or mission-driven organisations would be an advantage.
· Practical knowledge of applying AI tools in communications work is preferred.
· Excellent command in spoken and written English & Chinese (including Putonghua).
· Proficient in computer applications including MS Office and Chinese word processing.
· Good understanding of Oxfam’s beliefs and values on poverty alleviation, sustainable development and humanitarian belief. Identification with Oxfam’s mission and vision is a must.

job.title: Legal Officer/ Manager
job.description:
We're looking for a dedicated Legal Officer with a passion for social justice to join our team in Hong Kong. This is a crucial role that combines legal expertise with project coordination and stakeholder engagement, focusing on advancing access to justice for migrant workers. If you're a proactive legal professional ready to make a tangible impact, we encourage you to apply.

This unique opportunity allows you to contribute to a mission-driven organisation, working at the intersection of legal support, community empowerment, and strategic development.

Applicants with strong relevant experience and background may be considered for a
Legal Manager position.

Key Responsibilities
1. Legal Casework Management
● Manage cross-border casework aligned with JWB’s mission
● Conduct outreach activities to raise awareness of JWB’s cross-border casework programme
● Support case team’s efforts in knowledge management and casework processes optimisation

2. Stakeholder Engagement & Communications
● Build and maintain collaborative relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, including law firms, NGOs, government agencies, and academic institutions
● Assist in content creation for communications materials, such as newsletters, social media posts, and website updates, to showcase our impact
● Manage volunteers to further JWB’s mission

3. Organisational Support
● Assist in writing grant proposals and preparing timely, accurate reports for funders
● As part of a small and agile team, provide flexible support to other organisational needs as they arise

Qualifications & Experience
1. Qualifications
● Bachelor of Law degree, or relevant degree/experience
● A minimum of 2 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in the non-profit sector, legal services, or a related field
● Language requirements: English and Chinese (Cantonese)
● Must have the right to live and work in Hong Kong

2. Personal attributes
● Passionate about improving the conditions of migrant workers
● Strong interpersonal skills and can work effectively and respectfully in a culturally diverse environment
● Willingness to take initiative and adapt to evolving challenges
● Self-directed and able to follow through on tasks and responsibilities independently

Terms of engagement
● Full-time
● 15 days paid annual leave, in addition to public holidays
● Remuneration:
○ Legal Officer: HKD19,500 – 22,500 per month
○ Legal Manager: HKD 23,000 – 26,000 per month
● Occasional overseas travel may be required as part of our work
● Professional development and coaching opportunities included

How to Apply
Are you ready to build a world where justice has no borders?

Please send your CV/resume and a cover letter to celine@forjusticewithoutborders.org with the subject line: “Application: Legal Officer – [Your Name]”. The cover letter should describe your interest in working with JWB and spell out your relevant educational and practical experience. We accept applications on a rolling basis. Please note that only complete applications will be considered.

Justice Without Borders is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of race, gender, disability, religion, sexual orientation, or national origin

job.title: Development & Fundraising Officer
job.description:
Enrich is the leading Hong Kong charity promoting the economic empowerment of migrant domestic workers.

The Development & Fundraising Officer, reporting to the Development Manager, supports fundraising, donor relations, and campaign coordination to expand Enrich's educational programs and advance its mission. The primary objective is to help secure funding and build donor partnerships. The Development & Fundraising Officer will help research and write grants, coordinate impact monitoring and reporting, support campaigns and events, and track grant finances.

Job Overview
● Role: Development & Fundraising Officer (Part-Time, 3-4 days a week)
● Sector: Non-Profit / Financial Literacy
● Reporting To: Development Manager
● Objective: Support fundraising, donor relations, and campaign coordination to expand Enrich's mission.

Core Responsibilities
Grant Research & Writing Support
● Research Opportunities: Assist in identifying and researching funding opportunities with foundations and corporate partners aligned with Enrich's mission.
● Draft Applications: Help draft application materials, proposals, and project outcome summaries under the guidance of the Development Manager.
● Handle Administration: Support vital development administration, including preparing donor acknowledgement letters and donation receipts.

Impact Monitoring & Reporting
● Gather Feedback: Collaborate with the programmes team to gather qualitative and quantitative feedback, photos, evidence, and powerful impact stories from programme participants.
● Draft Reports: Assist in drafting accurate, compelling progress reports for funders that clearly demonstrate project outcomes and social return.

Campaigns & Event Coordination
● Support Communications: Support communication efforts for the Individual Giving programme, including writing thank-you acknowledgements and drafting engaging updates for donors.
● Coordinate Events: Help coordinate fundraising events, corporate employee engagement activities, and Enrich's participation in external functions.
● Manage CRM Data: Manage corporate volunteer sign-ups and maintain clean, up-to-date records in our CRM database to support seamless relationship management.

Track Grant Finances
● Ensure Compliance: Ensure restricted funds are spent according to grant requirements.

Position Requirements
Experience & Education
● Educational Background: A degree in Marketing, Public Relations, Business Administration, Non-Profit Management, or a related field.
● Professional Experience: Professional or practical experience in sales, marketing, communications, or fundraising preferred.

Technical & Soft Skills
● Passion & Values: Anchored in personal integrity and a strong sense of empathy, championing the financial empowerment and rights of migrant domestic workers in Hong Kong.
● Communication: Fluent in written and spoken English; Chinese language skills are a strong plus.
● Technical & Digital Literacy: Competent IT skills, including MS Office Suite, Google Workspace, and familiarity with AI tools, with basic graphic design capabilities (e.g., Canva or Adobe) and/or website content management experience as distinct advantages.
● Work Style: Detail-oriented, highly organized, and eager to learn; combines the ability to drive results independently during remote workdays with active, enthusiastic participation in collaborative team settings.

job.title: Data Analyst (Measurement, Evaluation and Learning)
job.description:
Bei Shan Tang Foundation is a private philanthropic foundation founded in 1985 to enhance global understanding of Chinese culture through traditional art and art history. Alongside this mission, since 2014 we have committed significant resources to transforming education in Hong Kong through Positive Education — cultivating resilience, inspiration, and collaborative communities grounded in evidence-based practices. 

We empower students to embrace change, thrive, and lead purpose-driven lives. Through collaborations with schools and esteemed institutions locally and worldwide, we introduce pedagogical innovations and effective strategies for educators. We also provide scholarships for students with financial needs to pursue studies abroad, nurturing Hong Kong’s next generation of leaders.

The role
Reporting to the Director (Education), you will serve as the Foundation’s quantitative expert — ensuring our education initiatives are grounded in rigorous evidence and our impact is clearly understood. You will own the full data cycle: from designing measurement approaches and managing longitudinal datasets through statistical analysis, interpretation, and translating findings into clear insights for diverse audiences. While you will work independently on technical analyses, you will collaborate closely with colleagues to ensure every analysis addresses meaningful questions that matter for students, educators, and the Foundation’s mission.

Key responsibilities
Measurement and insight generation
  • Design for understanding: Translate research and evaluation questions into appropriate quantitative measurement frameworks, adapting or developing tools that capture what matters in education and wellbeing initiatives.
  • Build the evidence base: Establish, maintain, and manage multi-wave and longitudinal datasets from the Foundation’s research, evaluation, and education programs, ensuring data quality and accessibility.
  • Analyze with rigor: Select and apply appropriate statistical methods — including descriptive statistics, psychometric analysis, group comparisons, regression, and longitudinal modeling — based on research questions, measurement characteristics, and data structure.
  • Uncover what matters: Identify meaningful patterns, trends, and findings that support continuous improvement of the Foundation’s education and wellbeing programs.

Communication and impact
  • Translate complexity: Prepare clear summaries of analytical findings across multiple formats — spreadsheets, tables, infographics, and written reports — ensuring technical accuracy without sacrificing accessibility.
  • Bridge worlds: Interpret statistical findings and communicate their implications and limitations clearly to non-technical colleagues, helping them make informed decisions.
  • Share learning: Contribute to deliverables that promote public awareness and engagement, including presentations, reports, and academic papers that advance the field.

You may also contribute to knowledge management within the Foundation and assist in facilitating education-related professional development offerings. 

Who you are
We value how you approach your work as much as what you know. The strongest candidates will recognize themselves in the following:
  • You believe data is a tool for positive change, not an end in itself. You are driven by curiosity about what helps students thrive and educators succeed.
  • You balance rigor with pragmatism. You apply sophisticated methods when they add value, but you also know when a simpler approach tells the story more clearly.
  • You are a careful listener and clear communicator. You ask questions to understand what colleagues truly need, and you explain complex findings in ways that empower rather than confuse.
  • You are systematic and detail-oriented, but you never lose sight of the bigger picture — the students and educators whose lives our programs touch.
  • You are intellectually honest. You report findings accurately, acknowledge limitations openly, and view unexpected results as opportunities to learn.
  • You are deeply curious about Hong Kong’s education system and genuinely motivated to contribute to its improvement. 

What you’ll bring
  • A bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Data Science, Psychology, Education, Social Sciences, or a related quantitative discipline (postgraduate qualification preferred).
  • 2–5 years of experience in data analysis, quantitative research, program evaluation, or educational/social research, with a track record of independently conducting rigorous analyses.
  • Strong proficiency in SPSS, R, or Python, with demonstrated ability to conduct descriptive statistics, psychometric analysis, group comparisons, regression, and longitudinal or repeatedmeasures analyses.
  • Solid understanding of research methodology, quantitative analysis, and measurement principles. Experience with multi-wave or longitudinal datasets is an advantage.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and systematic approach to data quality, statistical analysis, and interpretation.
  • Experience in data visualization and workflow automation is a strong asset.
  • Proficiency in English and Chinese; ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.

Terms and benefits
This is a one-year fixed-term contract, renewable based on mutual agreement and operational needs. We offer competitive remuneration commensurate with experience, a 5-day work week, compensatory leave for weekend work, compassionate leave, comprehensive medical and dental insurance, and annual health checkups.

How to apply
Bei Shan Tang Foundation is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Fresh graduates with relevant skills are encouraged to apply; experience in education and psychology is an advantage.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter indicating your earliest starting date and expected salary to Ms. Erica Yam (Senior Programme Manager) at ericayam@beishantang.org with “Application for Data Analyst (Measurement, Evaluation and Learning)” in the subject line.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Programs & Operations Manager / Director (Hong Kong)
job.description:
PILnet is an international, locally present non-governmental organization (NGO) that partners with legal professionals and social purpose organizations (SPOs) globally to protect civic space, address global challenges, and work to build just, equitable, and sustainable societies. PILnet does this by supporting civil society, engaging legal professionals, and nurturing the next generation of legal professionals in three strategic priority areas: civic space, climate justice, and people on the move. PILnet currently has offices in New York, Budapest, and Hong Kong, but operates globally.

PILnet Hong Kong works with SPOs, legal professionals, and law students to (i) strengthen the legal capacity and resilience of the social sector and (ii) strengthen pro bono culture in Hong Kong. PILnet Hong Kong’s main services for SPOs include its Pro Bono Clearinghouse and its Legal Health Check service. Through these services, PILnet Hong Kong connects SPOs with pro bono lawyers, helping them access high-quality legal expertise that would otherwise be out of reach. On strengthening pro bono culture, PILnet Hong Kong works closely with law students as the next generation of lawyers. Through providing mentorship, internships, and other learning opportunities, PILnet Hong Kong highlights the importance of public interest law and pro bono work, instilling in law students a long-term commitment to supporting the social sector. PILnet Hong Kong further strengthens pro bono culture by regularly convening lawyers, through events such as the Hong Kong Pro Bono Roundtables, to explore different ways in which they can support public interest causes. PILnet Hong Kong is guided by its Board of Directors, with half of its board members based in Hong Kong.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Based in Hong Kong and reporting to the Co-Executive Director, who is based in Asia, the Programs & Operations Manager/Director (Hong Kong) will oversee the design and execution of all projects in Hong Kong and ensure the smooth operations of the office. They will work with a team of legal officers and program staff, ensuring that the Hong Kong program remains relevant to local stakeholders and aligns with PILnet’s mission. They will also work closely with the rest of the PILnet team and other colleagues across PILnet’s offices to design and implement cross-border strategies and projects. The Programs & Operations Manager/Director (Hong Kong) will be responsible for the following areas:

Programs:
- Oversee the successful and timely implementation of projects focused on Hong Kong in accordance with relevant grants;
- Conduct team meetings to discuss regular project tasks and issues;
- In consultation with the Co-Executive Director and the development team, investigate and explore new opportunities that align with PILnet’s vision and strategy;
- Keep the Co-Executive Director updated on developments related to Hong Kong programs and staff matters; and
- Coordinate sessions and other activities in preparation of PILnet’s annual Global Forum held in a different city each year.

Partnerships:
- In consultation with the development team, manage, deepen, and strengthen relationships with Hong Kong based funders;
- Support the Co-Executive Director and the development team in writing grant proposals, financial reports, donor reports, and other reports as necessary;
- Build partnerships with local stakeholders, such as public interest law organizations, government, corporations, and universities; and
- Represent PILnet at external events.

Legal, Governance and Finance:
- Ensure that the Hong Kong program operations and activities adhere to internal policies;
- In consultation with the Global Senior Counsel, support the Co-Executive Director in ensuring that PILnet Hong Kong is compliant with relevant laws and regulations;
- In consultation with the Global Senior Counsel, review agreements with external vendors, suppliers, and partners, including law firms and foundations, as necessary;
- Support the Co-Executive Director in managing and documenting PILnet Hong Kong board meetings; and
- Support the Co-Executive Director in reviewing and executing financial transactions of the Hong Kong office, as reviewed and approved by the finance team.

People Management:
- Manage and collaborate with a team of legal officers, program officers, fellows, and interns, to provide guidance, input, and feedback;
- Manage and oversee the allocation of assigned team’s staff time to the relevant tasks and projects;
- Conduct performance reviews and wellbeing check-ins for direct reports;
- Lead or support staff recruitment and onboarding processes as requested by the Co-Executive Director; and
- Other tasks as required by the Co-Executive Director or other authorized individual.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS
• Degree in law, political science, international relations, public administration or related field. Preference will be given to applicants with a law degree.
• Fluency in written and spoken English. Proficiency in spoken and written Chinese (Cantonese) is highly desirable.
• 8-10 years of relevant work experience, preferably in the legal nonprofit or public interest law field, and/or a graduate degree in a relevant field combined with relevant experience. Candidates with less relevant experience will be considered as Managers.
• Strong interest in public interest law, social justice and human rights.
• Project management experience and a record of delivering projects on time and to budget.
• Proactive, creative and opportunity-driven mindset.
• Excellent organizational and leadership skills, including setting and executing multiple projects simultaneously.
• Ability to work well under pressure and manage competing priorities whilst maintaining a professional approach.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills, demonstrated by the ability to present effectively and persuasively.
• Excellent people skills, including networking, organizing, negotiating, and inspiring.
• Strong ability to delegate tasks effectively and mentor program staff, fellows and interns.
• Social impact measurement and data analysis experience.
• Working knowledge of performance evaluation techniques and key metrics.
• Proficient in Microsoft Suite (Excel, Outlook, Access, etc.) and Google Apps. Advanced knowledge of excel and data visualization tools will be an advantage.

LOCATION & CONDITIONS
You will work alongside a small multicultural team from nonprofit management and legal backgrounds, providing you with a supportive and flexible working environment. The nature of the position mandates that the prospective candidate is based and has the right to work in the Hong Kong SAR. PILnet is not in a position to facilitate working visas and work permits.
This is a full-time position or a part-time (min. 60% capacity) position. The position will involve some regional and international travel, essential to the implementation of PILnet’s activities. It is not expected to be more than 15 days per year cumulatively.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS
Interested candidates should submit their application package via an online form as well as through recruitment@pilnet.org with the subject line “Programs & Operations Manager/Director (Hong Kong)” by October 9, 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis as soon as applications are received. The application package must include:
- Submitted online form
- Resume or CV
- Cover letter (max 1 page)

The cover letter should describe your interest in working with PILnet and spell out your relevant educational and practical experience. We kindly request that applicants do not submit resumes with pictures. PILnet focuses solely on qualifications, skills, and experience relevant to the consultancy requirements. job.title: Operations Associate
job.description:
Founded in 2017, Resolve Foundation is an award-winning Section 88 charity dedicated to empowering changemakers. Our vision is to create a Hong Kong where everyone belongs and upholds inclusion. Despite being a global city, 1 in 8 people in Hong Kong report experiencing discrimination (EOC, 2021). We believe we all can be empowered to actively change this, in big and small ways.

Our mission is to amplify marginalized voices, empower diverse changemakers and build intersectional communities to elevate our collective social impact. Our values stand for Resolve: Rights, Equality, Solidarity, Organization, Leadership, Voice and Empowerment. Our organizational culture emphasizes: diversity, learning, responsibility, collaboration and gratitude. Learn more: resolvehk.org.

About the Role
The Operations Associate will serve as the operational anchor of Resolve’s daily administration, working in close coordination with and directly reporting to the Operations Director. In this capacity, you will maintain robust, efficient administrative, human resources, financial, and facility systems that keep our team supported and our organization running seamlessly. This position is an initial 12-month full time contract, with renewal subject to performance and funding

Key Job Duties
1. Internal Finance Support & Bookkeeping Assistance
● Digital Accounting System Support : Act as the primary contact point for day-to-day bookkeeping with the external accounting firm.
● Internal Helpdesk & Reimbursements: Assist team members' inquiries regarding financial workflows; guide staff accurately through spending approval and reimbursement processes.
● Petty Cash Oversight: Maintain, disburse, and thoroughly log the physical and digital office petty cash funds for minor daily expenses.
● Budgeting & Grant Tracking: Assist the Operations Director with various financial reports and grant tracking
● Audit, Procurement, & Compliance: Facilitate the procurement processes for the team. Maintain official organizational registrations, and compliance filings.

2. Human Resources Operations & Culture
● Employee Lifecycle Logistics: Administrative setups for onboarding new hires, coordinating offboarding logistics for existing staff, and keeping digital personnel files continuously secure and compliant.
● HR Metrics & Leave Tracking: Maintain comprehensive tracking of staff attendance, statutory/annual leave, and sick leave logs. Expand data maintenance to encompass general internal HR metrics.
● Employee Engagement Surveys: Administer, distribute, and collect responses for the Annual Employee Engagement Survey, helping synthesize feedback data for management.
● Payroll & Benefits Support: Accurately assemble and prepare monthly payroll sheets, Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) contribution drafts, and general benefits data for final director sign-off.
● Recruitment Coordination: Partner closely with hiring managers to post job listings, screen incoming resumes against criteria, assemble screening binders, and coordinate interview schedules.

3. Office Administration, Facilities & IT Support
● CRM System Optimization: Administer and maintain our CRM system. Actively research, map out, and propose structural workflow enhancements to elevate how our internal operations utilize CRM infrastructure.
● Front-Line IT Helpdesk: Provide basic, essential IT assistance to internal team members (including email setups, password updates, and software licensing access requests).
● Third-Party IT Liaison: Serve as the primary operational link and point of contact with our external, third-party IT support vendor to resolve technical issues quickly.

4. Internship Program Management
● Intern Recruitment: Lead talent acquisition by collaborating with institutes and organizations
● Intern Onboarding and Offboarding: Manage the complete lifecycle of the interns, including their comprehensive onboarding and formal offboarding processes.
● Intern Experience: Communicate with program line managers to ensure that every intern gains real project ownership and meaningful career development opportunities.

Essential Skills & Requirements
● Experience: Open to motivated fresh graduates demonstrating strong layout management capabilities through internships, or candidates with 1–3 years of experience in bookkeeping, administrative, HR support, or organizational operations roles. Experience within the non-profit or NGO landscape is a distinct advantage.
● Core Competencies: Exceptional organizational habits, sharp attention to detail, strict data confidentiality maintenance, and a service-oriented mindset.
● Technical Literacy: Tech-savvy profile with fluent command over cloud productivity suites (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) and foundational human resources software platforms.
● CRM and Accounting System Proficiency: Practical experience using CRM and accounting system; exposure to Odoo and Xero are highly beneficial.
● Language Fluency: Professional verbal and written proficiency in both English and Cantonese to manage local vendor transactions and partner communications.

Location
Sheung Wan, Hong Kong. Resolve allows for flexible working currently at a ratio of 40 (remote) /60 (in office).

Salary & Benefits
The expected salary for this role is $18,000 to $20,000 depending on experience. Note that Resolve has an established salary structure that is regularly reviewed against the market and set against a Competency Framework. Other benefits include flexible working and considerations for a balanced work-life relationship, health and dental insurance, opportunities for training and development, a culture of wellbeing and team-building, and above-market levels of annual leave. Resolve will provide you with a work phone and laptop. We are also based out of a larger social impact coworking space that has perks and organizes several activities and events.

Equal Opportunities
We believe a diverse and inclusive team is key to our success and social impact. We actively welcome and encourage applications from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, religion, or belief. As one of the first 100 signatories to the Racial Diversity & Inclusion Charter of the Equal Opportunities Commission, we are proud to be building a more equitable workplace. Your unique perspective is valued here and will make our nonprofit stronger. If you need any special assistance or accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know.

Application Process
Interested candidates in the role should apply on or before October 7, 2026. Should you have any questions on the position, or need any support, please email jobs@resolvehk.org. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted about the status of their application.

job.title: CHAIR, BOARD OF DIRECTORS
job.description:
The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong kong)

Our Purpose
We are determined to deliver Fred Hollows’ vision of preventing blindness and restoring sight.

Our priority is to work with communities to improve their own eye health. We do this through life-changing surgeries and treatments, training doctors and health workers, generating new ideas, and pushing for change at all levels – from local to global. The Foundation works in more than 25 developing in East Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa and Australasia.

The Fred Hollows Foundation (“The Foundation”) established the Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) over a decade ago, and together with other international organisations in the United Kingdom, Kenya and the United States of America, the international organisations form a global network to support the work of The Foundation. The Foundation’s latest Annual Report is available here[SB1]  and the Global Strategy 2024-2028 is available here.

ROLE Purpose 
The Chair leads The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) (FHF (HK)) Board of Directors to achieve its aim: ending avoidable blindness and restoring sight to those in need.

Within the global Fred Hollows Foundation network, FHF HK plays a primary role in mobilising resources (as a ‘market entity’) to support sight-restoring work in low- and middle-income countries.

By 2030, FHF HK aspires to be The Foundation’s trusted catalyst of resourcing for the Greater China Region, unlocking resources, partnerships and influence to scale eye health equity across Asia. FHF HK will do this by serving as The Foundation’s regional philanthropy hub in Greater China, mobilising capital (donations, institutional philanthropy and investment), partnerships and influence across Hong Kong and Macau to scale eye health impact.

The Chair plays a critical role in ensuring effective governance leadership, strong strategic oversight, and alignment with The Foundation’s vision of a world in which no one is needlessly blind. The Chair also leverages their networks to unlock access to prospective significant supporters and facilitates engagement with priority stakeholders and events that would not otherwise be accessible to FHF HK.

With the term of the current Chair concluding at the end of November 2026, it is suggested that a new Chair be appointed in the lead up to the expiry of the current Chair’s term.

Role of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) Chair
The Chair of the Board of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) is appointed by the Board of Directors, with Directors approved by the Global Board of the sole member (The Foundation).
The Chair serves for two three-year terms. Directors may serve a maximum of nine consecutive years. The powers of Directors, the Board and its Chair are set out in the Articles of Association and the Corporate Governance Charter.

The Chair is expected to:
  1. Ensure, in partnership with the Board, that FHF HK’s strategy is aligned with The Foundation’s Vision and Strategy, and that goals are achieved with integrity.
  2. Promote the values and goals of The Foundation in all aspects of governance and engagement with members, employees, partners, governments and communities.
  3. Perform duties in alignment with The Foundation’s Charter, the Articles of Association and relevant law, ensuring FHF HK operates in an ethically, environmentally and socially responsible manner.
  4. Lead the Board with tact and diplomacy, promoting a culture of integrity, respect, transparency, collaboration, resourcefulness and compliance.
  5. Chair Board meetings to ensure they are effective, efficient, and support high-quality, ethical decision-making.
  6. Commit sufficient time to the role, including representing FHF HK at donor, corporate, government and community engagements, and providing access to professional and philanthropic networks.
  7. Build a productive working relationship with management, including the Head of Market Hong Kong and Macau and relevant Global teams, including setting Board agendas.
  8. Engage with The Foundation’s initiatives to evolve global governance frameworks.
 
Essential Experience
  1. Demonstrated experience to Chair the Board.
  2. Demonstrated ability to implement and oversee governance, integrity and compliance processes at a board level.
  3. Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change.
  4. Demonstrated ability to develop substantial philanthropic, business or corporate fundraising networks and relationships on behalf of The Foundation and take part in high level meetings.
Desirable Experience
  1. Demonstrated experience negotiating and partnering with not-for-profits, corporations, governments, multi-lateral and other non-government agencies in pursuit of The Foundation’s goals and interests.
  2. Understanding of how a brand is perceived in the market and execution of brand management
  3. Experience working with an international health and development organisation.
  4. Demonstrated understanding of working with developing countries and human rights.
  5. An established public profile known for credible authentic leadership with access to high level decision makers in government and industry
Skills
1.    Strategic leadership and organisational stewardship.
2.    Governance, financial and risk oversight expertise.
3.    Effective board leadership and facilitation.
4.    Political acumen, influence and relational leadership.
5.    Sharp analysis and sound judgment in complex and ambiguous environments.
6.    Diplomacy, negotiation and partnership capability.
7.    Ability to operate across diverse cultures and contexts.

Qualifications
Relevant qualifications in leadership and Company Directors Course and MBA or Bachelor of Commerce/Economics/Business Management/Political Science/Law degree or equivalent.

Attributes
  1. Strong commitment to The Fred Hollows Foundation’s vision and values. 
  2. Hong Kong residency preferred; experience in international or cross-cultural organisations desirable. 
  3. Mandarin language proficiency preferred but not essential.

Safeguarding
The Chair will be required to undertake training and sign up to the standards set for conduct by The Foundation, the Australian Government’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian NGO Co-operation Program and the Australian Council for International Development. This includes child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

Travel
Domestic and International travel may be required as part of this role.
Time Commitment 
  • Up to four Board meetings per year (two hours).
  • Up to one budget briefing per year (1-2 hours).
  • Up to two International Organisation meetings per year (1-2 hours).
  • Ongoing agenda setting and governance preparation.
  • Regular stakeholder engagement, including donor, partner and advocacy events.

Term of Appointment 
Appointed for an initial term of three years, renewable once by mutual agreement between FHF HK and The Foundation for a maximum term of 6 years. 

APPOINTMENT STRUCTURE
Board Director roles for The Foundation are voluntary (unpaid). The role offers the opportunity to contribute at a strategic level to a globally recognised organisation, shaping the growth of the Hong Kong market and enabling eye health programs that restore sight and transform lives and communities globally.
